Quality Defect Root Cause Study - Meridian Parts

Study period: April 2024 - September 2024 (6 months)
Total units produced: 847,000
Total defects reported: 12,312 (1.45% overall defect rate)
Target defect rate: 0.8%

Defect rates by line:
- Line A (stamping): 1.12% (3,247 defects / 289,800 units)
- Line B (welding): 2.31% (3,891 defects / 168,500 units)
- Line C (assembly): 1.67% (2,814 defects / 168,400 units)
- Line D (finishing): 0.73% (1,360 defects / 186,300 units)
- Line E (new, started June): 2.89% (1,000 defects / 34,000 units - small sample)

Root causes identified:

Line B (worst performer, welding):
- Primary cause: weld temperature inconsistency (62% of defects)
- Contributing: worn fixtures causing misalignment (23% of defects)
- Other: operator error, material variance (15%)
- Fix: replace temperature controllers ($180K) + new fixtures ($95K) = $275K
- Expected defect reduction: to 0.9-1.1%
- Timeline: 4 weeks for parts, 1 week install

Line E (new line, finishing issues):
- Primary cause: tooling not calibrated to spec (71% of defects)
- Contributing: operator training gaps (29%)
- Fix: recalibration ($45K) + training program ($22K) = $67K
- Expected defect reduction: to 1.2-1.5% (still learning curve)
- Timeline: 2 weeks

Line C (assembly):
- Primary cause: supplier component variance (54% of defects)
- Contributing: assembly sequence not optimized (31%)
- Fix: supplier quality enforcement (negotiation ongoing, unclear cost) + process redesign ($110K)
- Expected defect reduction: to 1.0-1.2% if supplier cooperates, 1.3-1.5% if they dont
- Timeline: 8-12 weeks

Line A (closest to target):
- Primary cause: die wear (58% of defects)
- Fix: scheduled die replacement program ($210K over 12 months)
- Expected defect reduction: to 0.7-0.85%

Unknowns: we dont know if Line E's issues are just startup problems that will self-resolve or if there's a fundamental tooling design problem. Also Line C's supplier (Vantage Components) is our only source for 3 of those parts so we cant just switch - we dont know how receptive theyll be to tighter tolerances without a price increase.

Tom needs to prioritize which lines get investment first given we have about $400K budget this quarter.

Fleet Electrification Feasibility Study - Northland Logistics

Current fleet: 284 vehicles
- 156 delivery vans (Class 2-3)
- 84 regional trucks (Class 4-6)
- 44 long-haul trucks (Class 7-8)

Electrification option - Phase 1 (delivery vans only):
Replace 156 delivery vans with electric equivalents

Vehicle cost:
- Electric van: $78K each vs $52K for diesel = +$26K per vehicle
- Total incremental cost: $4.06M
- Available incentives: $1.24M (federal + state)
- Net incremental cost: $2.82M

Charging infrastructure:
- Depot charging (4 depots): $890K for 80 Level 2 chargers + 12 DC fast chargers
- Electrical panel upgrades: $340K
- Total infrastructure: $1.23M

Operating cost savings (estimated):
- Fuel savings: $1.1M/year (electricity vs diesel at current prices)
- Maintenance savings: $420K/year (fewer moving parts, less brake wear)

Charging timeline:
- Level 2 full charge: 8 hours (overnight at depot)
- DC fast charge: 1.5 hours to 80%
- Current routes: average 120 miles/day, max 180 miles
- Electric van range: 150-200 miles depending on load and weather

Risks:

Model Monitoring Gap Assessment - Aether Analytics

Assessment date: October 2024
Scope: all production ML models serving customer-facing and internal products

Total production models: 67

Monitoring coverage:
- Fully monitored (performance + drift + data quality): 18 (26.9%)
- Partially monitored (performance only): 23 (34.3%)
- Minimally monitored (basic uptime only): 14 (20.9%)
- No monitoring: 12 (17.9%)

Coverage by model criticality:
- Tier 1 (revenue-impacting, 14 models): 10 fully monitored, 3 partially, 1 minimally
- Tier 2 (customer-facing but not direct revenue, 22 models): 5 fully, 12 partially, 3 minimally, 2 none
- Tier 3 (internal decision support, 31 models): 3 fully, 8 partially, 10 minimally, 10 none

Gaps identified:

Gap 1 - Feature drift detection: Only 9 of 67 models have feature drift monitoring. This means 58 models could have input distribution shifts without detection. For Tier 1 models, 4 of 14 lack drift detection.

Gap 2 - Prediction quality monitoring: 26 models have no automated way to detect if predictions have degraded. We rely on manual checks or customer complaints.

Gap 3 - Data quality checks: Only 12 models validate input data before scoring. Bad data (nulls, out-of-range values, schema changes) can produce silently wrong predictions.

Gap 4 - Bias/fairness monitoring: Zero models have bias monitoring. This is not currently required by regulation but is a known emerging risk.

Proposed monitoring rollout:
- Phase 1 (Q1 2025): Add drift + data quality to all Tier 1 models, add prediction quality to remaining Tier 1 models
  Cost: $85K (infrastructure) + 320 engineering hours
  Timeline: 8 weeks

- Phase 2 (Q2 2025): Extend to all Tier 2 models
  Cost: $60K + 280 engineering hours
  Timeline: 6 weeks

- Phase 3 (Q3 2025): Tier 3 models + bias monitoring pilot on 5 Tier 1 models
  Cost: $45K + 240 engineering hours
  Timeline: 8 weeks

Total cost: $190K infrastructure + 840 engineering hours (approximately 5.25 FTE-months)

Risks of not monitoring:
- We had 2 incidents in 2024 where model degradation went undetected for 3+ weeks. One caused an estimated $340K in mispriced recommendations before discovery.
- Regulatory risk is increasing - the EU AI Act requirements start phasing in 2025 and we sell to EU customers.

Unknowns: we dont know the exact engineering capacity available in Q1 because 2 of our 6 MLOps engineers may be pulled into a platform migration project. Also unclear whether the bias monitoring pilot needs legal review before deployment, which could add 4-6 weeks.

Sanjay needs to decide: approve full rollout starting Q1, delay to Q2 to resolve capacity questions, or approve Phase 1 only and reassess.
